job: Let users ask the agent to triage and open issues in their repositories
summary: GitHub is one of the easier providers. You can register an OAuth app in a few minutes with no review, and it works for any GitHub user right away. The main decision is OAuth App vs GitHub App, since GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for finer-grained permissions.

verdict.difficulty_reason: Self-serve registration, no app review for OAuth apps, works for all users immediately.
verdict.approval_wait: None from GitHub. Restricted orgs need an owner's approval.

composio.note: This is canned demo data. In live mode the agent checks Composio's docs.

paths.name: Use Composio managed OAuth
paths.when_to_choose: Prototyping, or you don't need your own branding on the consent screen.
paths.tradeoffs: Consent screen shows Composio's app, not yours.

paths.name: Register your own GitHub OAuth App
paths.when_to_choose: You want your own branding or need to control scopes.
paths.tradeoffs: OAuth App scopes are coarse (e.g. repo grants full repo access).

paths.name: Register a GitHub App
paths.tradeoffs: Different install flow; users install the app on repos.

needs.ok_if: Any email works; GitHub sends a code to confirm it.

needs.item: Owner rights, if the app should belong to an organisation
needs.ok_if: Not needed if the app lives on your personal account.
needs.later: Org-owned apps need an org owner to approve.

actions: Enter your email, a password and a username.
Type the code GitHub emails you.
prerequisites.done_when: You can sign in and see your GitHub dashboard.

needs.item: A Google or GitHub login, or an email

actions: Sign in with Google or GitHub.
prerequisites.done_when: You can see the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Open GitHub developer settings
steps.detail: Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App.
steps.done_when: You can see the 'Register a new OAuth application' form.

steps.title: Register your GitHub app
steps.detail: Fill in application name, homepage URL and authorization callback URL. Use the callback URL your platform (e.g. Composio) gives you, exactly as shown.
steps.done_when: The app page shows a Client ID.
actions: Enter your app's name and website.
Paste the **callback URL** from Composio, then click **Register**.

steps.title: Save your app's secret
steps.detail: Generate a client secret, copy it once, and store it with the Client ID in your secrets manager or Composio auth config.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are saved somewhere other than your clipboard.
actions: Copy the **Client ID** and secret into Composio.

steps.title: Pick the permissions you need
steps.detail: For issue triage: 'repo' for private repos or 'public_repo' for public only. Request nothing else.
steps.done_when: Your scope list is written down and matches the job.
steps.agent_prompt: My agent needs to read and open issues in my users' GitHub repositories. List the minimum GitHub OAuth App scopes for that, explain each in one line, and tell me if public_repo is enough when users only have public repos.
actions: Paste the prompt below into your coding agent.
Check its answer lists only what your agent needs.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.detail: Authorize with a test account and call the Issues API once.
steps.done_when: An API call returns your test repo's issues.
steps.agent_prompt: Write a short script using the Composio SDK that connects a test GitHub account through my GitHub auth config and lists the open issues in one repository. Print the result so I can see the connection works.
actions: Paste the prompt below into your coding agent.
Run the script it writes and sign in with a test account.

steps.title: Get org approval (some orgs)
steps.detail: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions must approve your app before members can use it with org repos. Send the owner a request from the authorization screen.
steps.done_when: The org shows your app as approved.
actions: Ask the GitHub org owner to approve your app.
Wait for their OK; carry on with other work meanwhile.

scopes.why: Read and write issues in private repos

approval.process: No GitHub review for OAuth apps. Orgs with OAuth app access restrictions require an org owner to approve your app.
approval.wait: None, or however long the org owner takes

blockers.mitigation: Tell users how to request org owner approval, or use a GitHub App installed on the org.

alternatives: Fine-grained personal access tokens for single-user tools
agent_can_do: Pick minimal scopes for your job
you_must_do: Sign in to GitHub and create the app
next_action: Decide whether Composio's managed OAuth is acceptable for launch. If yes, you can skip registration entirely.

sources.title: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
Scopes for OAuth apps - GitHub Docs

route.name: Register your own GitHub OAuth App
route.reason: Demo data: you said the sign-in screen must show your brand, so you register your own app. It's self-serve and has no review.
route.wait: None, unless an org restricts OAuth apps

costs.item: Composio plan for your users' connections

glossary.plain: The registration that tells GitHub your product exists and is allowed to ask users for access.
The web address GitHub sends users back to after they approve access; it must match exactly.
A public name tag for your OAuth app.
A password for your OAuth app; keep it private.

friction_checks.answer: Demo data: a GitHub account needs only an email, username and password, plus an email code.
Demo data: no. OAuth apps live under Settings → Developer settings on any account.

friction_checks.check: Which app type and required fields?
friction_checks.answer: Demo data: OAuth App; needs a name, homepage URL and callback URL. Any URL you own works as the homepage.

friction_checks.check: Is the secret shown only once?
friction_checks.answer: Demo data: yes, copy it right away; you can generate a new one later.
Demo data: none; org-owned repos may need org approval.
Demo data: no review for OAuth apps.
